_source: Every product name and price below is taken verbatim from the Brandywine Fisheries online store (brandywinefisheries.com/shop), fetched 2026-08-17. Prices change — the site notes that the counter is authoritative. Third-party brands (Ekone, Jose Gourmet, Matiz, Arroyabe, Season, California Girl, St. Ours, Rose City Pepperheads, Pacific Seafood) are goods Brandywine resells, not products they make.

categories.name: Smoked Fish
categories.blurb: Brandywine's own smokehouse line — applewood and alderwood. Thirteen items, and the part of the case that travels best.

items.name: Smoked Salmon
items.note: The flagship of the smoked line and the most expensive item in it by weight.

items.name: Smoked Peppered Salmon
items.note: Same cure, heavy cracked pepper crust.

items.name: Smoked Steelhead
items.note: Milder and sweeter than the salmon.

items.name: Smoked Peppered Steelhead
items.note: The peppered treatment on the sweeter fish.

items.name: Smoked Black Cod (Sablefish)
items.note: The highest-oil fish in the case, which makes it arguably the best candidate for smoke of anything here.

items.name: Smoked Tuna Loin
items.note: Albacore loin, smoked whole.

items.name: Smoked Teriyaki Lingcod
items.note: A lean fish that takes a glaze rather than a dry cure.

items.name: Smoked Teriyaki Rockfish
items.note: The least expensive smoked fillet in the line.

items.name: Smoked Salmon Collars and Wings
items.note: The collar is the fattiest cut on the fish and the one most cooks never see.

items.name: Smoked Jalapeno Salmon Sausage Links
items.note: Sold by the dozen online, individually at market.

items.name: Smoked Oysters
items.note: The least expensive item in the smoked line.

items.name: Smoked Seacuterie Board
items.note: The largest single item Brandywine sells — a full board of the smoked line.

categories.blurb: Never frozen. Iced on the boat from the point of catch, which is the whole argument for buying it here.
